items.title: USN-8709-1: ncurses vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that ncurses incorrectly handled specially crafted
terminfo database entries. A local attacker could possibly use this issue
to cause applications using ncurses to crash, resulting in a denial of
service.

items.title: USN-8708-1: sudo-rs vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that sudo-rs incorrectly handled time-of-check vs time-
of-use conditions in sudoedit. A local attacker with permission to edit
specific files using sudoedit could use this issue to place files in
arbitrary directories, and possibly escalate their privileges. This issue
only affected systems configured to grant fine-grained sudoedit file
editing permissions, which is not the default configuration.

items.title: USN-8690-1: Pillow vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Pillow did not properly manage memory when
processing certain image files. An attacker could possibly use this  issue
to cause a denial of service or read sensitive data.

items.title: USN-8705-2: OpenZFS vulnerability
items.summary:
USN-8705-1 fixed vulnerabilities in OpenZFS. This update provides the
corresponding fix for OpenZFS on Ubuntu 18.04 LTS and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.

Original advisory details:

It was discovered that OpenZFS incorrectly handled authorization checks for
certain ioctl operations on Linux. A local attacker could possibly use this
issue to perform pool-administrative operations or access privileged
information, resulting in an authorization bypass.
